caseName: SIREN, et al. v. City of San Jose
summary: EFF and the ACLU of Northern California sued San Jose on behalf of the Services, Immigrant Rights and Education Network (SIREN) and the Council on American-Islamic Relations - California (CAIR-CA), alleging the city's nearly 500 ALPRs and year-long data retention let officers search a year's worth of any driver's movements without a warrant, violating the Fourth Amendment and the California Constitution's privacy protections. Reporting on the lawsuit cited 261,711 warrantless searches of San Jose's ALPR database between June 2024 and 2025. A separate federal class action over San Jose's ALPR use, brought by three residents with the Institute for Justice, is also pending.
whyItMatters: San Jose's system - nearly 500 cameras with a full year of retention - is one of the largest single-city ALPR deployments being challenged in court, and tests both the federal and California constitutional theories at once.
